title: CASE OF CALDARAR AND OTHERS v. POLAND
conclusion: Violation of Article 8 - Right to respect for private and family life (Article 8-1 - Respect for family life;Respect for private life)
summary:
In Caldarar and Others v. Poland, the applicants were five families of Romanian nationals of Roma origin, including nine adults and seven children, who settled on municipal land at Paprotna Street in Wrocław. Their case concerned the vulnerability of Roma families living in informal settlements and facing eviction without adequate safeguards. The families began occupying the site around November 2009, erecting makeshift wooden and plastic cabins that served as their homes. Polish authorities repeatedly informed them that their occupation was illegal and, in May 2013, issued formal orders requiring them to vacate and clean up the land. Subsequent inspections found the structures to be unsafe, lacking basic utilities, and at risk of fire or collapse. Demolition orders were issued in September 2013, and the cabins were eventually destroyed, resulting in the loss of the applicants’ possessions.

Throughout this period, the applicants were offered temporary accommodation in shelters and municipal hostels, but they declined these options, citing unsuitability for their families’ needs. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Article 8 of the Convention, which protects the right to respect for private and family life. The Court found that the demolition of the applicants’ homes, without sufficient consideration of their specific circumstances and without providing genuinely suitable alternative accommodation, constituted a violation of Article 8. This judgment highlights the need for authorities to balance urban regulations with the fundamental rights of vulnerable Roma families facing eviction.
